bib.title: AttnGAN: Fine-Grained Text to Image Generation with Attentional Generative Adversarial Networks

read.skipped: Supplementary material is not in the PDF (only a link).

question: Can word-level attention in a multi-stage text-to-image GAN, plus a fine-grained image-text matching loss, give better and better-conditioned images than conditioning on a single sentence vector?
hypothesis: Conditioning only on a global sentence vector lacks word-level detail; attending to relevant words per image sub-region and adding a word-level matching loss should improve quality, especially on complex scenes.
contributions: An Attentional Generative Adversarial Network with two components: the attentional generative network and the DAMSM.
A comprehensive empirical study showing it significantly outperforms previous state-of-the-art GAN models.
A detailed analysis visualising the attention layers, showing the layered conditional GAN attends to relevant words.

method.summary: A 3-stage generator (64, 128, 256 px) where stages after the first query word vectors with an attention layer per image sub-region. A pretrained DAMSM (BiLSTM text encoder + Inception-v3 image encoder) gives a word-level matching loss added to the GAN loss with weight lambda.

datasets.name: CUB
datasets.source: Wah et al. 2011, preprocessed as in StackGAN [31]
datasets.preprocessing: preprocessed according to the method in [31]

models.name: AttnGAN1
models.architecture: one attention model, two generators (64 and 128 px)

models.name: AttnGAN2
models.architecture: two attention models stacked with three generators (64, 128, 256 px), one discriminator per scale

models.name: DAMSM text encoder
models.architecture: bi-directional LSTM; word vector is concatenation of two directions' hidden states; sentence vector is concatenated last hidden states

models.name: DAMSM image encoder
models.architecture: Inception-v3 up to mixed_6e (local 768x289 from 768x17x17) and last avg pool (global 2048), plus a new perceptron layer into the common space
models.init_from: Inception-v3 pretrained on ImageNet, layers fixed

training.objective: L = sum_i L_Gi + lambda * L_DAMSM; per-stage adversarial loss with unconditional and conditional terms; discriminators trained with cross-entropy; DAMSM loss = word-level plus sentence-level matching losses in both directions, pretrained separately on real image-text pairs
training.epochs: curves in Fig 3 run to about 550 epochs (CUB) and 150 (COCO); read from Fig 3

other.lambda: 0.1, 1, 5, 10 searched on CUB; 0.1, 1, 10, 50, 100 on COCO; chosen by raising lambda until validation inception score starts to drop
other.DAMSM_hyperparameters: gamma1=5, gamma2=5, gamma3=10, M=50 (set on a held-out validation set)
other.DAMSM_applied_to: output of last generator only; applying on all resolutions did not help and cost more compute
other.DAMSM_pretraining: on real 299x299 images; finetuning it with the whole network did not improve performance
other.not_tried: three attention models, due to GPU memory constraints

inference.samples: 30,000 images generated from randomly selected unseen text descriptions per model for inception score and R-precision

metrics.name: inception score
metrics.definition: Salimans et al. 2016 measure, following StackGAN

metrics.name: R-precision
metrics.definition: generated image queries 100 candidate descriptions (1 ground truth, R=1, plus 99 random mismatches); cosine similarity of global vectors from the pretrained DAMSM encoders; r/R

eval.protocol: Inception score on 30,000 generated images with +- as printed; R-precision uses the paper's own DAMSM encoders, which are also used in training the proposed model. Lambda chosen on a held-out validation set. Seeds and number of runs not stated. Qualitative attention visualisation.

results.claim: AttnGAN raises the best reported COCO inception score from 9.58 to 25.89.
results.setup: COCO test set, AttnGAN2 lambda=50, 256x256, vs PPGN
results.quote: our AttnGAN boosts the best reported inception score on the COCO dataset from 9.58 to 25.89, a 170.25% improvement relatively.
results.note: Table 3 prints 25.89 ± .47; the best baseline in the comparison is PPGN (9.58 ± .21); StackGAN is 8.45

results.claim: AttnGAN reaches inception score 4.36 on CUB, above the previous best 3.82.
results.setup: CUB test set, AttnGAN2 lambda=5, vs StackGAN-v2
results.quote:
our AttnGAN achieves 4.36 inception score, which signif-
icantly outperforms the previous best inception score of
3.82.
results.note: abstract and conclusion print the relative gain as 14.14%

results.claim: Removing the DAMSM (using the text encoder of Reed et al.) drops CUB R-precision to 10.37% and inception score to 3.98.
results.setup: CUB, AttnGAN1 without DAMSM vs AttnGAN2 lambda=5 (67.82)
results.quote:
the
inception score and R-precision drops to 3.98 and 10.37%,
respectively
results.note: R-precision std printed as 5.88 for this row; no-DAMSM row is AttnGAN1 and the baseline_value row is AttnGAN2, so not a like-for-like pair

results.claim: On CUB, raising lambda from 0.1 to 5 raises AttnGAN1 R-precision from 16.55% to 58.65%.
results.quote:
the inception score of the AttnGAN1 is improved from 4.19 to 4.35
and the corresponding R-precision rate is increased from
16.55% to 58.65%

results.claim: Final COCO model reaches R-precision 85.47% at lambda=50.
results.table: Table 2, row AttnGAN2 lambda = 50 (COCO), column R-precision(%)
results.note: R-precision is computed with the DAMSM encoders trained with the model's own loss, so it favours models trained with that loss

results.claim: Stacking a second attention model (128 to 256 px) gives slightly higher inception score on CUB (4.35 to 4.36 at best lambda) and higher R-precision (63.87 to 67.82 at lambda 10 vs 5).
results.setup: CUB, AttnGAN2 lambda=5 vs AttnGAN1 lambda=5
results.table: Table 2, row AttnGAN2, lambda = 5, column inception score
results.note: difference 0.01 is within the printed ± .03 to .04

limits: The model sometimes generates sharp, detailed but unrealistic images (birds with multiple heads, eyes or tails); global coherent structure is not captured.
COCO images are not as photo-realistic as CUB.
Three attention models not tried because of GPU memory.
Optimizer, learning rate, batch size, epochs and hardware are not stated; supplementary material is only a link.
R-precision uses the authors' own DAMSM encoders, also used in training; no human evaluation; evidence for attention is qualitative visualisation.
Inception score is the headline metric; the authors concede it does not show whether an image matches the text.

terms.definition: Deep Attentional Multimodal Similarity Model: learns to map image sub-regions and words into a common space to compute a fine-grained image-text matching loss

lineage.note: stacked multi-stage GAN conditioned on a global sentence vector; Conditioning Augmentation and data preprocessing reused
joint conditional/unconditional loss and structurally disjoint discriminators

lineage.work: GAN-INT-CLS (Reed et al., Generative adversarial text-to-image synthesis)
GAWWN (Reed et al., Learning what and where to draw)

the GAN in their framework was only utilized as a
post-processing step without attention
